choices.title: Progressive patient care
choices.correct_explanation:
• Patient care method in which patient care areas provide various levels of care Progressive patient care.
  • Progressive patient care Units also called intermediate care or step-down units, provide a transition between the ICU and the general unit or discharge.

Case method

Nursing care delivery model where one nurse provides total care for one patient during the entire work period; it is the oldest method of providing care to a patient.

Team method

Team nursing is a system that distributes the care of a patient amongst a team that is all working together to provide for this person. This team consists of up to 4 to 6 members that has a team leader who gives jobs and instructions to the group

Primary care method

It is also called relationship-based nursing. It involves total nursing care, directed by a nurse on 24-hour basis as long as the client is under the care.

Progressive patient care

Progressive patient care Units also called as intermediate care or step-down units, provide a transition between the ICU and the general unit or discharge.

 

Reference:

True experimental research designs are those where researchers have complete control over the extraneous variables and can predict confidently that the observed effect on the dependable variable is only due to the manipulation of the independent variable. A true experimental research design must essentially consist of the following three characteristics:

o   Manipulation refers to conscious control of the independent variable by the researcher through treatment or interventions to observe its effect on the dependent variable.

o   Control refers to use of control group and controlling the effects of extraneous variables on the dependent variable in which researcher is interested.

o   Randomization is used to minimize the threat of internal validity of the study and to eliminate the effect of extraneous variables on dependent variables.

·         The Hawthorne effect is the inclination of people who are the subjects of an experimental study to change or improve the behavior being evaluated only because it is being studied and not because of changes in the experiment parameters or stimulus. The Hawthorne effect refers to the fact that people will modify their behavior simply because they are being observed.

·         So, the true experimental research design must contain a control group, a variable that can be manipulated by the researcher, and the distribution must be random.

Reference:

    1. Management of nursing services and education, I Clement, pp. 296-97.

choices.correct_explanation:
• The ethical principle which shows obligation, to tell the truth, is veracity.
    • Ethical principles: Principle of respect for autonomy, Principle of non-maleficence, Principle of beneficence, Principle of justice, Principle of veracity, etc.
    • Autonomy: Refers to the right to make one’s own decisions.
    • Fidelity: It means to keep a promise.
    • Beneficence: Refers to taking positive actions to help others.

Reference:

    1. Kaur L, Kaur M. Textbook of Nursing Foundation, 3rd edition; 2017. p. 60

choices.title: Fever with Chills, chest tightness
choices.correct_explanation:
• Fever with Chills, chest tightness describes the expected side effects associated with the first dose of muromonab-CD3.
    • Muromonab-CD3 is a mouse monoclonal antibody to CD3, often refereed as OKT3, which is used to treat acute cellular rejection after organ transplant. Common side effects are fever and chills, chest pain, diarrhea, muscle joint pain etc.
    • Other options are distractors.

Reference:

    1. https://www.mayoclinic.org, [Accessed February 2019]

questions.title: The nurse is caring for a child who is experiencing acute renal transplant rejection. Which of the following most accurately describes the expected side effects associated with the first dose of muromonab-CD3?

choices.title: Your daughter has acrocyanosis; this is causing her blue hands and feet
Let’s watch her carefully to make sure she does not have a circulatory problem
This is normal; her circulatory system will take a few days to adjust
choices.correct_explanation:
• The parents of a 2-day-old girl baby areconcerned because her feet and hands are slightly blue, the nurse should respond that “This is normal; her circulatory system will take a few days to adjust”.
    • It is not an abnormality, but rather a minor immaturity of the circulatory system, which will be resolved after some time.
    • Acrocyanosis is persistent blue or cyanotic discoloration of the extremities. Acrocyanosis have marked clamminess and hyperhidrosis of hands and feet, which tend to worsen in warmer temperature while the color change improves. It is treated with oxygen administration.
    • The child will have other systems with blue discoloration like dyspnea, tachypnea, and other infections. Explaining about the circulatory problem to parents will also cause fear and anxiety.
    • Vasomotor changes refer to vasodilation and vasoconstriction. But the child may have an immature circulatory system.

Reference:

    1. www.https://www.webmed.com, [Accessed July,2017]

choices.title: Note any blanching of the skin
Lightly tap the area where the cream is
choices.correct_explanation:
• Lightly tapping the area where the cream is applied is the correct way to assess whether the cream has achieved its purpose or not.
    • Eutectic mixture of local anesthetics (EMLA) (a combination of prilocaine and lidocaine) is an example of a cream applied to the site 30–60 minutes before the procedure. Used in minor surgeries.
    • The effectiveness can be achieved by lightly tapping the area where the cream is applied because tapping sensation of that area can be assessed.
    • Skin redness is a sign of infection.
    • Blanching indicates a temporary obstruction in blood flow, poking can be a part of the procedure.

Reference:

    1. Lewis’s medical surgical nursing, 1st edition; 2011. pp. 357-58

choices.title: Gently poke the individual with a needle

questions.title: The nurse has applied EMLA cream as ordered. How does the nurse assess that cream has achieved its purpose?

choices.title: Notify the doctor immediately
choices.correct_explanation:
• The nurse should notify the doctor immediately.
    • Compartment syndrome is a serious complication of casting and splinting. It occurs when there is increased pressure within a confined space which compromises blood flow and low tissue perfusion occurs. Ischemia and irreversible neuromuscular damage can occur. 6 Ps of compartment syndrome is pain (not relieved by opioid analgesics), pressure, paresthesia, pallor, paralysis, pulselessness.
    • The first action should be to notify the physician. Applying ice and elevating the arm will worsen the condition further.
    • Giving additional medication will not help because it is mentioned that the pain is not relieved by prescribed medications.

Reference:

    1. Lewis’s medical surgical nursing, Vol 2, pp. 1582-83

choices.title: Give additional pain medication as ordered

questions.title: An 8-year-old girl was diagnosed with a closed fracture of the radius at approximately 2 PM. The fracture was reduced in the emergency room and her arm placed in a cast. At 11 PM her mother brought her back to the emergency room due to unrelenting pain that has not been relieved by the prescribed narcotics. What should the nurse do first?

choices.title: Flush the tube
choices.correct_explanation:
• Flushing the orogastric tube just after administering the medication is a priority nursing action to prevent the clogging of the tube.
    • Because of the small diameter of the tube, and when drugs are not thoroughly crushed or dissolved in water,orogastric tubes are prone to obstruction. Failure to flush the tube before and after both drug administration can result in tube clogging, which may necessitate removal and insertion of a new tube. The patient must receive the prescribed dose of medication. The tube is flushed to administer the drug completely.

Reference:

    1. Lewis’s Medical Surgical Nursing, Vol. 2, p. 937

questions.title: A nurse has just administered medication via an orogastric tube. What is the priority nursing action?

choices.title: They can mask signs of infection
choices.correct_explanation:
• The nurse carefully monitors the condition of a child because the nurse is aware that corticosteroids can mask signs of infection.
  • Corticosteroids control the immune response, metabolic pathways, fluid and electrolyte balance, the cardiovascular and central nervous systems.
  • Corticosteroids work by reducing the activity of the immune system, so they may also mask or hide some usual symptoms of infection. A child should avoid people with infections, avoid crowded places, etc.
  • Corticosteroids do not affect liver enzymes; do not cause bone marrow suppression.

References:

  1. Lewis’s medical surgical nursing, 1st edition; 2011. p. 1646
  2. https://www.aboutkidshealth.ca, March 21, 2010

questions.title: The nurse is caring for a child who is taking corticosteroids for systemic lupus erythematosus. The nurse carefully monitors the child’s condition because the nurse is aware that corticosteroids can have what major action?

choices.title: Mark the tracheal tube at the child’s lip
Watch for yellow display on CO2 monitor
choices.correct_explanation:
• The nurse would assess for yellow display on the CO2 monitor. Capnography is a non-invasive method for monitoring the level of CO2 in exhaled breath to assess a patient’s ventilatory status. It has become a standard of care. The CO2 detector should change color from purple to yellow.
  • Auscultation of chest sounds is performed rather than abdominal breath sounds. Auscultation will help in checking the equal air entry in both the lungs which will ensure the correct position of ET tube. Auscultation of abdominal sounds is used to assess the abnormal bowel sounds.
  • Marking the tracheal tube at the child’s lip will help in determining the length of the insertion of the tube.
  • According to the studies inspect for the presence of water vapor is an unreliable method because condensation can be present in both cases if the tube is correctly positioned in the trachea or if the tube is in the oesophagus.

 Reference:

  1. Lewis’smedical-surgical nursing, 1st edition; 2011. pp. 1680-82

choices.title: Inspect for water vapor in the tracheal tube

questions.title: Which measure would be most appropriate for the nurse to do to ensure that a child’s ET tube is correctly positioned?

choices.title: Pulse oximetry
choices.correct_explanation:
• For 8 years old with tachycardia and tachypnea pulse oximetry can determine the extent of hypoxia.
    • Pulse oximetry is a method by which arterial oxygen can be monitored non-invasively and continuously using a pulse oximeter probe on a finger or toe.
    • PFT: a non-invasive test that measures lung volume, capacity, rates of flow, and gas exchange. It is a complete evaluation of the respiratory system.
    • Peak expiratory flow: Maximum speed of expiration as measured with a peak flow meter.
    • Chest X-ray: It is a projection radiograph of the chest used to diagnose conditions affecting the chest. It is used to screen changes in the respiratory system.

Reference:

    1. Lewis’s medical surgical nursing, 1st edition; 2011. pp. 514, 518-19.
